text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with a generalized rash; to help you, I need to ask a few questions. First, how old are you in days, and when did the rash first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Since the rash appeared on day 4 of life and the mother has a history of gonorrhea, we need to rule out early-onset infection. Do you notice any redness around the umbilical cord or signs of poor feeding like lethargy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a maculopapular rash with pustules on an erythematous base, sparing the palms and soles, is highly suggestive of Neonatal Lupus Erythematosus. Given your mother's history of untreated gonorrhea, I must also rule out early-onset sepsis. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, C-Reactive_Protein, and Blood_Culture. Do you have any swelling in the wrists or ankles?
